en: 9. The Question on the Factor of the Laborer “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘one factor of a laborer should be adopted,’ which is that one factor that should be adopted?
“Great King, just as a laborer thinks thus: ‘I am a hired hand; I am doing work for this ship.’”
‘By the labor of rowing this boat, I receive my food and wages; I must not be negligent;
with diligence must this boat be rowed by me.
In the same way, Great King, a practitioner, a follower of yoga, should reflect thus: ‘This body of mine, composed of the four great elements…’
‘Contemplating the body constantly and continuously, being diligent, with mindfulness established, mindful, clearly comprehending, concentrated, and one-pointed in mind,
I shall be liberated from birth, aging, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; therefore,
“Great King, this is one quality that should be adopted from the laborer.
This was also said, Great King, by the Elder Sāriputta, the General of the Dhamma:
having seen the true nature of the body,
you shall make an end of suffering."
The ninth question: on the factor of action.
